newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Bangemann paper on Internet regulation close to adoption.
newsitem.headline: Bangemann paper on Internet regulation close to adoption.

text.p: The European Commission may adopt next week a communication drafted by Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann on ways to tackle illegal and harmful material on the Internet, Commission officials said on Tuesday.
The paper is meant to complement a green paper on new media services being drafted by Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja.

However, there is a chance the paper could be adopted first if the green paper is delayed because the Commission is under a deadline to produce concrete proposals on the Internet before the November Telecommunications Council, they said.
EU sources said previously that a turf battle between Oreja and Bangemann had delayed the green paper, originally scheduled to be adopted this week.

The officials said the two papers would have some overlap since they will both deal with protection of minors. However, Bangemann's paper will look at other questions such as how to prevent copyright violations or the use of the Internet to promote terrorism, they said.
The paper will endorse the idea of a global conference on how to regulate the Internet and other information networks that Germany has offered to host.
